items.title: No local estimate of working alarms by tenure
items.whyItMatters: Targeting the giveaway needs the size of the renter and owner gap in this county, and the figure quoted locally has no traceable source.
items.opportunity: Estimate prevalence by tenure and heating type from a probability sample this winter.

items.title: Self-report overstates working alarms
items.whyItMatters: Tested alarms were far fewer than reported ones (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Verify alarms with the test button and record siting and manufacture date.

items.title: Nonresponse differs by tenure
items.whyItMatters: Renters answer telephone surveys far less often (claim c3), so a low-response sample would overstate prevalence.
items.opportunity: Door-to-door fieldwork with up to three visits and weighting by segment and dwelling type.

items.title: Households least able to act on an alarm
items.whyItMatters: Seasonal agricultural workers with limited English, people with hearing loss and older people living alone may have alarms they cannot hear or cannot replace.
items.opportunity: Offer information in the main local languages, record hearing-related needs, and link households to fitted alarms with visual alerts.

items.title: Giveaway reaches households who ask
items.whyItMatters: Request-based delivery misses renters, who made up 12 percent of visits against 27 percent of households in one service.
items.opportunity: Use survey segments with the lowest prevalence to plan proactive visits.

errorsFound: The 40 percent figure quoted locally has no traceable source and should not be used as a planning value.
A model lead presented the retrieved national survey as a landmark with an identifier that the record does not carry.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm a probability-based door-to-door survey with verification, stratified reporting by tenure and heating type, and nonresponse handling as the core of the study.
summary: Five gaps; the high-severity ones are the missing local estimate and the bias of self-report.
